A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original FineWeb and CodeParrot training experiments, downstream benchmark results, learned tokenization examples and downsampling analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including Table 1 benchmark outcomes, validation-loss curves and appendix tokenization analyses.

M1.justification: The stated boundary policy in Eq. 21 changes its history sum from j=1,...,w to j=1,...,w-1. Consequently, the w=1 variant changes from conditioning on the preceding boundary to byte-only logits. This is a limited revision of the specified policy; the PDFs do not establish that its implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb and CodeParrot and report the same PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, LAMBADA and held-out FineWeb evaluations. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Uniform, Dynamic (Nawrot et al.), H-Net (Hwang et al.) and BPE guidance on FineWeb, and H-Net on CodeParrot. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 2.5 revises the reported w=1 experimental configuration from using the immediately preceding boundary to using no boundary history. This changes the stated setting without establishing a rerun. Data processing, metrics, training budgets and Appendix D hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing window ablation is redefined as removing boundary-history dependence entirely, rather than retaining one preceding boundary. Its reported measurements are unchanged. The aspect-ratio analysis, convergence analysis and tokenization case studies are retained without additional evidence.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same standard-error reporting convention. Neither version adds or removes run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted curves and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 1 still reports FineWeb Test values of 1.280 ± 0.003 for Ours (w=1) and 1.297 ± 0.003 for Ours. The revised window specification is not accompanied by revised scores.

T1.justification: Equations 4 and 7–9 correct inconsistent mathematical definitions: mid receives X', downsampling selects byte representations X_i, and upsampling adds token representations Y'_j. Equation 21 also corrects the projection index and history-sum bound. The score-function derivation and Appendix A proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about learning semantic token boundaries with variance-reduced score-function estimation, outperforming straight-through estimators and supporting different downsampling rates.

C2.justification: Section 2.5 changes the takeaway from the ablation: v2 says a large window is unnecessary, whereas v3 says the boundary-history window and sequential scan are not strictly required. Other interpretations, applicability limitations and future-work discussions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 2.5 newly specifies that the scan following precomputed linear projections is sequential and runs on the CPU. Previously its execution location was unspecified. Appendix D, the hyperparameter tables and the code-release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3, Appendix C and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to heuristic tokenization, straight-through estimators and concurrent reinforcement-learning work is retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits in Sections 2.2 and 2.5 correct function names and byte/token terminology, clarify causal attention and rewrite the window-computation explanation. Section ordering, the broader narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–3 retain their graphics, captions, structure and placement, including all appendix displays. There is no display addition, removal, redesign or relocation; the edits cause only incidental local text and equation reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects inconsistent tensor inputs and byte/token mappings in Eqs. 4 and 7–9, making the architecture easier to understand and implement. The corrected boundary-policy expression and CPU-scan disclosure also improve technical precision. These are limited gains in specification and reproducibility guidance; the empirical evidence is unchanged, and no implementation change or rerun is established.
